description.narrative: Enhancing Georgia's capacities to comply with the Paris Agreement's Enhanced Transparency Framework.

Global Environment Benefits and co-benefits This CBIT project is designed to generate global environmental and socio-economic co-benefits. This project enhances national capacities to accurately track, report, and verify climate data. The project supports enhanced reporting and assessments in national GHG inventories, mitigation, vulnerability, and adaptation to climate change impacts, as well as NDC tracking and tracking support needed and received. This will help to ensure Georgia becomes fully compliant with the ETF of the Paris Agreement. The access to more reliable data and improved reporting will also improve the information provided to the Global Stocktake, enhancing the overall capacity to track the actual progress towards the long-term temperature goals of the Paris Agreement. The project will support the development of long-term climate strategies in Georgia. The National Transparency Platform will act as the repository of knowledge and information that will inform future decision-making. Output 3.2 includes piloting the integration of the NTP into climate planning and policy, which provides for developing a roadmap, protocols, and tools. By establishing a reliable data collection, analysis, and dissemination system, the project could increase NDC ambition and positively impact policies and plans in other sectors like energy, agriculture, etc. The project will enhance Georgia's capacity to report to other non-UNFCCC MEAs, such as the SDGs, allowing for a streamlined approach across the country's international reporting commitments. By strengthening institutional frameworks, such as national transparency units and data management systems, these projects ensure that climate actions are well-informed, coordinated, and transparent. In addition, the project will generate multiple co-benefits. The project implementation will strengthen Georgia’s institutional and technical capacity by forming a new Transparency Working Group and multiple training initiatives. The project includes a capacity-building programme, with the main beneficiaries being training participants. The participants will consist of a range of stakeholders, including government agencies, the private sector, NGOs/CSOs, and others as listed in REF _Ref153632132 \h \* MERGEFORMAT Table 30 08D0C9EA79F9BACE118C8200AA004BA90B02000000080000000E0000005F005200650066003100350033003600330032003100330032000000 . At the technical and operational level, it will lead to the development of relevant policy instruments that will inform and guide the formulation of cost-effective project proposals in all four ETF modules. At the institutional level, the project will strengthen national coordination frameworks and involve the main stakeholders in implementing the ETF, thereby enhancing policy integration in Georgia. By enhancing stakeholder engagement, including government agencies, private sector actors, and local communities, the CBIT project promotes inclusivity and collaboration in climate decision-making. In the absence of this project, there will be an uncoordinated approach to transparency, as several ongoing initiatives ( REF _Ref174454980 \h \* MERGEFORMAT Table 7 08D0C9EA79F9BACE118C8200AA004BA90B02000000080000000E0000005F005200650066003100370034003400350034003900380030000000 ) are being delivered in parallel without an overarching framework for transparency. At the environmental level, the project will give Georgia a clearer idea of the impact of climate change on its territory and its mitigation, adaptation, and support needs. It will also show activities where intervention may result in further co-benefits and support broader national objectives for sustainable development. The NTP will provide better access to climate change information to develop well-informed viable strategies to increase resilience in Georgia, which is increasingly at risk of extreme weather events due to climate change, which has implications for the economic, social, and psychological welfare of vulnerable communities. Responding effectively and timely to these risks requires the strategic combination of updated information and decision-making, thereby creatively linking the expertise, efforts, and actions of diverse stakeholders, including local government, scientists, industry experts, and communities. The CBIT 2 project will provide a social benefit, including gender-responsive approaches, ensuring equal participation and benefiting marginalized groups in climate-related planning and actions. The CBIT 2 Project will also benefit Georgia economically, as improved transparency attracts international climate finance by demonstrating accountability and readiness for investments in mitigation and adaptation projects. The CBIT 2 project will contribute to regional and global knowledge sharing. This project will accelerate the dissemination of best practices and innovations in transparency systems by facilitating peer learning and collaboration among countries. Without GEF support, the government would lack the technical expertise, institutional capacity, and resources necessary to implement these comprehensive transparency Platforms. The additionality of this project is evident in its ability to elevate national efforts, enabling countries to contribute more effectively to global climate goals, improving the accuracy of international reporting, and fostering global cooperation on climate change. These benefits are critical for advancing global environmental stewardship and enhancing adaptation efforts in the face of escalating climate challenges.
